answer.location_description: A thin horizontal band spanning the full image width near the top edge, at rows 2-3 and columns 0-23. It lies well outside the central nodule region.
answer.shortcut_type: Bright horizontal line or band artifact near the top border
answer.mechanism: About 14 first-layer units (0, 3, 5, 12, 13, 14, 15, 18, 19, 20, 21, 23, 24, 28) carry strong, uniform positive weights across every column of rows 2-3. Units 9, 16 and 30 carry uniform negative weights there. Layer-2 unit u9 sums the positive group (weights 76-95 from units 3, 5, 13, 14, 23, 24) and is inhibited by units 9, 16 and 30. Unit u12 does the same (97, 99, 86, 85 from units 14, 20, 23, 28; -93 from unit 16). Both u9 and u12 have negative output weights (-95 and -63). Unit u2, which takes units 9, 16 and 30 positively and the positive group negatively, has output weight +99. So brightness in rows 2-3 raises the benign pathway and suppresses the malignant pathway, pushing the logit toward benign.
answer.evidence: Rows 2-3 in units 3, 5, 14, 15, 18, 19, 20, 23, 24 and 28 are nearly all positive, typically +30 to +70 across all 24 columns. The rows directly above and below (r0-1, r4-5) are mixed or near zero, which defines a thin line detector. Units 16, 30 and 9 show the mirror pattern: rows 2-3 at -20 to -59 across the width, with positive rows 4-5. A full-width uniform band at a fixed row near the border is not a nodule property. Weaker, less consistent bands also appear in rows 18-19 and 22-23, but rows 2-3 are the most consistent.
answer.main_feature: The model contrasts nodule size and extent. Units with a small positive centre (rows 10-12, cols 10-13) and a negative surrounding ring respond to compact, small nodules and favour benign. Units 9, 16 and 30 respond positively to dense tissue across a wide central area (rows 4-17), indicating a large, irregular nodule, and favour malignant.
